symptom: Merged website obligations can remain nonterminal when their historical Required run failed only because an inherited baseline test asserted an implementation detail that was intentionally replaced by bounded concurrency.
root_cause: Terminal closure treated historical Required failure as permanently authoritative even after the merge was contained in newer main, the stale test was corrected, and live production was verified.
fix: Allow website-only descendant regression recovery when merge containment in current main is proven, the current-main website baseline plus bounded visibility regression is green, original BRAIN and applicable CodeQL remain green, and production readback remains mandatory.
prevention: Do not equate a stale verifier assertion with a live product defect.
Never rewrite historical Required failure as exact-head success.
Recover only through contained current-main regression evidence.
Keep original exact-head BRAIN and CodeQL evidence mandatory.
failed_approaches: Treating a historical Required failure as permanently terminal even after the merged change is contained in current main and the stale verifier assertion has been repaired.
Rewriting historical failed evidence as if the exact candidate had passed.
Opening duplicate recovery PRs instead of using contained descendant regression evidence.
